summary_1line: Discourse on virtuous conduct—truth, non‑injury, self‑control, charity—and the fowler’s karmic defense that destiny and past deeds shape one’s role in killing animals.

image_candidates.scene_text: A metaphorical river of life filled with shark‑like lust and temptation as a seeker rows a small boat of patience across the waters of the five senses.
King Sivi calmly slicing flesh from his own body to give to a supplicant, embodying extreme generosity.
The humble fowler speaking respectfully to a Brahmana while holding his hunting tools, explaining destiny and karma behind his violent trade.
